cost: Metadata and one-record city API queries worked without credentials or payment. Bulk-export arrangements and costs remain unconfirmed.
title: Property assessment lookup
publisher: City of New Haven — Assessor's Office; hosted by Vision Government Solutions
description: Look up properties in the assessor website or retrieve parcel identifiers, assessment values and property attributes through the city's public GIS API.
fields: Commercial unit count, stored as text
Residential unit count, stored as text
Condominium unit count, stored as text
Published sale date, stored as text
steps: Open the New Haven assessment database and read its valuation-date and disclaimer information before using the browser lookup.
Open the city parcel API metadata to inspect field names and types. An API is a web address a program can request to receive structured data.
Try the tested one-record JSON query: selected parcel and assessment fields, one record, and no geometry.
Use the Query operation with a where filter on parcel_id or property_address and select needed outFields. Match parcel and address identities carefully; tailored filters still need testing.

See related city GIS layers for address points and zoning. A possible lookup is address → location → parcel → assessment attributes, with zoning checked at the same location. Spatial matching still needs testing.
Confirm assessment details and valuation dates with the Assessor's Office. Vision is a separate HTML browser; no Vision assessment API has been verified.
contact: assessor@newhavenct.gov; contact appears in indexed official city page.
limitations: Live metadata and one-record JSON queries succeeded without API credentials on October 6, 2026. These checks establish technical access, not data accuracy, completeness or continued availability.
The city layers advertise a 1,000-record response limit and pagination. One response is not the full dataset.
Sample checks omitted geometry; spatial intersections, cross-layer joins, pagination, property-specific filters and bulk extraction remain untested.
Refresh schedules, reuse terms and field-code definitions remain unconfirmed. Layer edit timestamps do not establish the freshness of every record.
All 16 requested parcel fields were present in the live metadata and sample response.
The Vision landing page describes values as of October 1, 2021. The city GIS assessment valuation date is unconfirmed. Assessment values are not current tax bills.

Individual Vision property pages and field mappings have not been verified here. Extracting HTML from those pages would be page extraction, not a verified API, and can break when their structure changes.
